# Best slim Qi2 power banks for iPhone 17

**Best overall slim pick: Anker Nano Power Bank (5K, MagGo, Slim)**
- **Size and weight:** 0.34 in thick and 4.3 oz, with 5,000mAh of capacity.
- **Charging:** 15W Qi2 wireless, and Anker lists the iPhone 17 series as a fit.
- **Price:** $54.99 on Anker's site. Anker listed a $5 auto-applied discount that was ending soon.
- 9to5Mac says it's the closest alternative to Apple's own MagSafe battery and runs cooler than the competition.
- **Buy:** [Anker Nano Power Bank 5K](https://www.anker.com/products/a1665-5k-ultra-slim-qi2-power-bank)

**Slim and fast: INIU SnapGo Air (10,000mAh, 25W Qi2.2)**
- **Size and weight:** About 0.5 in thick and 195g, so it's thicker than the 5K models.
- **Charging:** 25W wireless, which the iPhone 17 supports, and 45W wired. It also has a built-in lanyard-style USB-C cable.
- **Price:** About $42.99 at Amazon and $44.99 at INIU, per Android Central.
- Macworld calls it an equal-slimmest 10K power bank, but it has no kickstand.
- **Source:** [Android Central review](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge). The search results didn't include a direct product link, so check the INIU or Amazon listing for the current price.

**Thinnest and lightest: Baseus Picogo Air AM71 (5,000mAh)**
- **Size and weight:** 0.27 in thick and 104g.
- **Trade-off:** Android Central lists wireless output at only 7.5W, so it will charge your iPhone 17 slowly.
- **Price:** $52.99 to $69.99 at Amazon.
- **Source:** [Android Central review](https://www.androidcentral.com/accessories/power-charging/i-tested-the-best-slim-qi2-power-banks-released-in-2026-baseus-torras-iniu-reelcharge)

## How to choose
- **Pocketability first:** Get the Anker Nano 5K. A 5K bank typically gives about 60–75% of a charge (Macworld).
- **More capacity and speed:** Get the INIU SnapGo Air. A 10K bank can charge a phone close to twice.
- **Only for maximum thinness:** Choose the Baseus Picogo Air, and accept the slow wireless speed.

The iPhone 17 supports 25W Qi2.2, so the Anker's 15W is a speed trade-off for its thinness.

**Optional:** Dealectric lists the Baseus PicoGo AM52 (10,000mAh, Qi2.2, 45W) at $53.99 with code AM52, tested in Baseus's cart on 2026-10-25. The results don't give its thickness, so I can't call it slim.
